source: National Guidelines and Minimum Standards for Child Development Centres in Sri Lanka
authority: Ministry of Women, Child Affairs and Social Empowerment

content.title: National Guidelines and Minimum Standards for Child Development Centres in Sri Lanka [cite: 1]
content.definition: A child development centre (children's home) is an organization providing love, protection, and accommodation to children looked after by persons other than their relations[cite: 171]. It must be licensed by the Provincial Department of Probation and Childcare[cite: 172].
content.target_group: Children defined as any person below 18 years of age[cite: 185].
objectives: Ensuring protection and developmental needs are met[cite: 161].

content.licensing_rules: Applicants must obtain a license or temporary permit before establishing a center[cite: 191]. Licenses are valid for 3 years[cite: 195].
content.management_committee: Must consist of at least five members, with at least three being permanent residents of the area[cite: 194].
content.rejection_criteria: If child safety is endangered or standards aren't met, the Provincial Commissioner can revoke the license and transfer children to safer locations[cite: 217, 218, 219].

content.hiring_standards: Staff must have prior approval from the Provincial Department of Probation and Child Care, renewable every 2 years[cite: 227]. Performance is reviewed after a 9-month probation[cite: 232].
content.manager_qualifications: Must be aged 30-60, a Sri Lankan citizen, and hold NVQ Level 6 in Child Development[cite: 255, 256, 260, 261].
content.caregiver_qualifications: Must be aged 22-60 and hold NVQ Level 4 in Child Development[cite: 279, 282].
content.gender_policy: Only female managers and caregivers are recruited for centers providing care for girls[cite: 233].
ratios: 1 staff member for every 5 children under age 5[cite: 314].
3 staff members for every 25 children over age 6[cite: 315].

content.first_aid: Every building must have a fully supplied, locked first aid box accessible only to staff[cite: 760, 762]. One staff member on duty must be trained in first aid for infants and children[cite: 768].
medical_monitoring: Children 0-5 years must be seen by Family Health Midwives; weight and height measured monthly[cite: 773].
Every child under 5 must have a health growth card[cite: 775].
Annual medical exams and bi-annual dental checkups are mandatory[cite: 778, 781].
content.nutrition: Daily menus must be displayed[cite: 619]. Food must be tailored to age, health, and religious needs[cite: 623, 626, 627].
content.immunization: Centers must refer children for age-appropriate immunization and maintain records[cite: 782].

content.physical_space: Each child requires 40 sq. ft. of internal bedroom space[cite: 536]. One toilet is required for every 8 children[cite: 560].
content.hazardous_substances: Drugs, tobacco, and toxic cleaning materials are strictly prohibited on premises[cite: 326, 719]. Furniture must be lead-paint free[cite: 728].
content.security: Centers must have a protective fence/wall and 24-hour security guards[cite: 676, 679].
content.sanitation: Waste must be sorted into separate bins: biodegradable, plastic, paper, and glass[cite: 751, 752, 753, 754].

prohibited_punishments: Physical punishment, emotional harassment, or psychological abuse are strictly forbidden[cite: 336, 924].
Depriving children of food, sleep, or medical care as punishment is prohibited[cite: 925, 926, 929].
Locking children in rooms or name-calling is prohibited[cite: 931, 939].
content.social_integration: Institutionalization is a last resort; economic problems are never a valid reason for admission[cite: 418, 420]. Child victims and juvenile offenders must be kept in separate centers[cite: 423].
content.education: Regular schooling is compulsory for children 16 years and under[cite: 879].

content.toilet_standards: One toilet must be provided for every 8 children[cite: 560]. Toilets should be mopped and kept dry to prevent slipping[cite: 573].
content.bath_facilities: At least one bathroom (with shower and wash basin) for every 10 children[cite: 577]. Separate facilities are mandatory for boys and girls[cite: 585].
content.water_safety: Centers must have an adequate supply of safe drinking water[cite: 639]. If using a well, it must be cleaned/emptied at least once a year[cite: 641].
content.potty_training: For infants, at least one potty for every three children is required[cite: 565]. Nappies are required for children under 2 years[cite: 563].

content.medication_storage: All medicines must be securely locked and inaccessible to children[cite: 811]. They must be kept in original packaging and clearly labeled[cite: 814].
content.medical_exams: A full medical examination is required within 2 weeks of a child's admission[cite: 792].
content.emergency_protocol: The nearest hospital must be identified for emergencies, and children must be transported immediately if urgent care is needed[cite: 785, 786].
content.malnutrition: Malnourished children must be referred to a nutrition center to improve their status[cite: 783].

content.infant_groups: Babies (4 months to 1 year) should be cared for in groups of maximum three babies per group[cite: 818].
content.feeding_safety: The temperature of prepared milk must be checked before feeding[cite: 824]. Feeding milk via a cup is recommended over bottles[cite: 826].
content.posture_care: While awake, an infant's or toddler's posture should be changed at least once every 30 minutes[cite: 821, 836].
content.toddler_stimulation: Sensory kinetic stimulation through singing, rhythmic actions, and nature-based play is required for ages 1-3[cite: 828, 830].

content.secondary_education: Children aged 11-18 should engage in activities for personality development, life skills, and leadership[cite: 860].
content.vocational_support: Children beyond compulsory education age should be referred to vocational training courses offered by recognized government institutions[cite: 862].
content.leaving_protection: Management must assist children in finding employment and suitable accommodation once they reach 18 years[cite: 484].
content.transition_monitoring: The Provincial Department of Probation must monitor children for at least one year after they leave the center[cite: 488].

content.lead_safety: Walls and furniture must not be coated with lead-based paints or toxic coatings[cite: 728].
content.fire_protection: Fire extinguishers in working condition must be available in every building[cite: 725].
content.hazardous_zones: Liquor outlets must not be located within 100 meters of the center[cite: 503]. Center must be free of unprotected wells, open ponds, and sharp objects[cite: 504].
content.animal_safety: Only cats, dogs, and fish are allowed as pets, and they must be properly vaccinated[cite: 699, 701].

content.anonymous_complaints: Children must be given the opportunity to make anonymous complaints or suggestions about staff or other children[cite: 964].
content.grading_system: Centers are categorized by color: Red (Immediate intervention/Serious threat), Yellow (Conditions to improve), and Green (Satisfactory).
content.inspection_frequency: The National Child Protection Authority (NCPA) performs annual monitoring of all centers[cite: 988].
content.staff_suspension: If a staff member is charged with abuse, they must be suspended and prohibited from the premises until the investigation is complete[cite: 972, 973].

content.child_personal_files: The Manager must maintain updated files for every child, including photographs, birth/age certificates, court orders, and immunization reports[cite: 387, 388, 391, 395].
content.mandatory_records: Centers must maintain a guests' log book, register of public officers, inventory, daily meal plans, and a complaints log[cite: 358, 359, 364, 368, 370].
content.access_control: Only the Manager, Probation Officers, and NCPA officials are permitted to access children's personal records[cite: 409].
content.medical_history: All chronic health problems, allergies, and developmental needs must be documented in the child's file[cite: 401, 403].

content.last_resort_policy: Institutionalization must only be considered as a last resort if all alternative options fail[cite: 418].
content.adoption_eligibility: For orphaned or abandoned children under 14, the possibility of adoption must be considered[cite: 428].
content.time_limits: Orphaned children under 14 should not stay in a center for more than two years; family reunification or foster care must be prioritized[cite: 431, 432].
content.emergency_admission: In emergencies, children may be admitted with written approval from the Commissioner, but a court order must be obtained within three working days[cite: 421, 422].

content.cpc_composition: The committee includes the Provincial Commissioner, Probation Officer, Child Rights Promotion Officer, and the child's parents/relatives[cite: 456, 457, 458, 461].
content.care_plan_timeline: A care plan to integrate the child back into society within 3 years must be prepared within two weeks of admission[cite: 465, 466].
content.child_involvement: The involvement of the child is mandatory when preparing their specific care plan[cite: 468].
content.review_frequency: The committee must meet every three months to review each child's development plan[cite: 469].

content.missing_child_protocol: If a child is missing, the Manager must immediately inform the police, parents/guardians, and the Child Replacement Committee[cite: 490, 491, 493, 495].
content.well_safety: Wells used for water must be kept closed when not in use; children must be supervised near them at all times[cite: 714].
content.electrical_safety: All wiring must be insulated, and electrical equipment in child-accessible areas must be covered[cite: 694, 696].
content.staircase_safety: Staircases used by infants and toddlers must be secured with a gate or door and have firmly fixed railings[cite: 740, 741].

content.court_transport: Court or police vehicles should not be used to transport children to court[cite: 685].
content.segregation_from_criminals: Children must not be transported together with adult criminals from police stations or prisons[cite: 686].
content.escort_requirement: The Center Manager or a childcare provider and the assigned probation officer must accompany the child to court[cite: 684].

content.mandatory_items: Each child must have a towel, at least 3 school uniforms, 4 sets of normal clothing, and 2 sets of bedding[cite: 706].
content.cultural_sensitivity: Clothing provided must be acceptable to the child's cultural values, religion, and gender[cite: 709].
content.laundry_facilities: The center must provide adequate facilities for washing clothes; staff must iron clothes for children under 14[cite: 710, 711].
content.personal_preference: Children's preferences must be taken into account when providing footwear and personal needs[cite: 705].

content.religious_integrity: A child's religion must never be changed before or after admission to a center[cite: 434].
content.celebrations: Facilities must be provided to celebrate Sinhala and Hindu New Year, Deepavali, Christmas, Vesak, Ramadan, and World Children's Day[cite: 914].
content.personal_milestones: Children must be given the opportunity to celebrate birthdays and personal achievements[cite: 916].

content.visitation_rights: Children are encouraged to contact parents and relatives; facilities for private meetings must be provided at reasonable times[cite: 941, 943].
content.confidentiality: Staff are obliged to protect all confidential information regarding children[cite: 251].
content.telephone_access: Children must have access to make or receive personal calls and mail from parents or friends recommended by the Probation Officer[cite: 953].
content.dignity_in_donations: Children should not be exposed directly to donors in a way that harms their dignity[cite: 955].

content.supervision_grading: Centers are assessed on a 10-point scale and categorized by color: Red (1-3.9), Yellow (4-6.9), and Green (7-10)[cite: 993].
content.red_category_action: Red category centers require immediate intervention and a follow-up inspection within two weeks[cite: 993, 997].
content.yellow_category_action: Yellow category centers require improvements and a re-supervision within 6 months[cite: 993, 1004].
content.green_category_action: Green category centers are satisfactory and subject to standard annual monitoring[cite: 993].

content.special_needs_placement: Children with special needs must be placed in centers that have the specific capacity to provide specialized care[cite: 435].
content.accessibility_law: Building designs must be accessible to children with disabilities in accordance with Disabled Persons Regulation No. 1 of 2006[cite: 533].
content.disability_equipment: Centers must provide necessary personal assistance, medicines, and equipment for children with disabilities[cite: 787].
content.education_for_disabled: Children with disabilities must be sent to appropriate schools or special education classes[cite: 882, 885].

content.substance_prohibition: Staff are strictly prohibited from bringing or using drugs, tobacco, or alcohol on center premises[cite: 326, 340].
content.role_modeling: Staff members are required to act as role models and maintain friendly, daily discussions with each child[cite: 323, 324].
content.confidentiality_breach: Failure to protect child privacy or perform duties satisfactorily is grounds for immediate termination of service[cite: 241, 251].
content.conflict_of_interest: Staff members are not permitted to work for or partner with any other child development center[cite: 311].

content.mandatory_recreation_items: Centers must provide at least three musical instruments, a television, a radio, board games, and art materials[cite: 900].
content.computer_policy: Computer use is limited to 45 minutes for learning purposes; internet access must be password protected with security precautions[cite: 905, 906].
content.reading_materials: A library suitable for the children's age is required, including daily newspapers and a weekly children's newspaper in the child's language[cite: 892, 895].
content.sports_safety: Every child should engage in outdoor or indoor sports daily, provided the weather is good[cite: 663].
